def-emg-matter-observables.physical_scope: Framework-local SI definitions of smooth matter fields, selected dust and perfect-fluid stress/current closures, and observer contractions in the equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model. It makes no empirical claim and supplies no general matter closure or coupled-field existence result.

def-emg-matter-observables:
## Definition

Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of the smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$ of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and metric-selected Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$. The exact tensor types, formal matter systems, stress convention, observer conventions and smoothness levels below are those of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Use SI units with length coordinates $x^0=ct$ as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]; no numerical value of the experimentally determined $\mu_0$ is treated as exact.

At a point $p\in\Omega$, an **observer** is a future-directed unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ satisfying $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth field of such vectors is an **observer congruence**. A tetrad is a basis of a tangent space; an observer, a congruence, a tetrad and a coordinate chart are different objects. A **four-velocity field** $U$ is a $C^2$ future-timelike vector field with $g(U,U)=-c^2$; $n=U/c$ is its unit observer at each point. A **proper-time worldline segment** is a $C^2$ future-directed timelike curve $z:I\to\Omega$ on an interval $I$ of proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $dz/d\tau=U$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$ along the segment. These are local model fields and curves; no global flow or completeness is included.

The matter variables are constitutive inputs of a selected model: rest-mass density $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, rest-charge density $\sigma$ in $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, rest-energy density $\epsilon$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and isotropic pressure $p$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. A smooth matter current $j^a$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and a symmetric matter stress tensor $T_m^{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ in the stated length-coordinate convention. Their physical meanings are fixed only after a constitutive branch is selected:

- For charged dust, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$. Here $\rho\geq0$ is rest-mass density, not energy density.
- For a perfect fluid, $T_m^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)U^aU^b/c^2+pg^{ab}$. Its rest-frame entries are $(\epsilon,p,p,p)$. No equation of state is included by this tensor definition.
- An optional conducting-fluid current is $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$, where $q^aU_a=0$ and $q^a$ is a rest-space conduction-current density in $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. The separate constitutive choice $q^a=\chi E_U^a$ uses a scalar conductivity $\chi\geq0$ in $\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$ and is not part of the general definition.

For a smooth real electromagnetic two-form $F$ and positive $\mu_0$, define the electromagnetic stress by

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

The components of $F$ in an orthonormal tetrad have tesla units. For an observer $n$, the observer electric field is $E_n^a:=cF^a{}_bn^b$ in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; with $U=cn$, write $E_U^a:=F^a{}_bU^b=E_n^a$. The observer magnetic field is the spatial covector $B_{n,a}:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$ in tesla, with the orientation and Hodge convention of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. These observer fields depend on $n$; they are not global observer-independent three-vectors.

Define the matter-plus-field force density by $f^a:=F^a{}_bj^b$, in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, and the matter exchange equation by $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=f^b$. This equation is a condition of a selected coupled model, not a consequence of the tensor definitions alone. For any unit observer $n$, define the measured energy density of a symmetric stress tensor $T_{ab}$ by $\mathcal E_n:=T_{ab}n^an^b$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Define its spatial energy-current vector by $\mathcal S_n^a:=-h_n{}^a{}_cT^c{}_bn^b$, where $h_n{}^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ projects to $n^\perp$; its orthonormal-frame physical energy flux is $c\mathcal S_n^i$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. These contractions are derived, observer-dependent quantities.

Within the selected Einstein–Maxwell formulation, the fields $g$ and $F$ may be dynamical unknowns in a coupled branch or prescribed data in a test branch. The matter variables $\rho,\sigma,\epsilon,p$ and any chosen conductivity or equation of state are independent constitutive input. The current, stress, force density, electromagnetic stress, observer fields and observer contractions are derived from those inputs by the displayed definitions. This definition makes no identification with Newtonian or thermodynamic quantities solely because units agree; it records no measurement and asserts no matter evolution, entropy law, or coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution.

post-emg-transported-charged-dust.physical_scope: A selected smooth single-stream charged-dust continuum in the equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model. It adopts the dust stress/current closure, undivided mass and force equations, and charge conservation; the ratio is transported only on positive-density domains. It does not assert coupled PDE existence, caustic avoidance, singular particles, or empirical validity.

post-emg-transported-charged-dust:
## Postulate

On an open region $\Omega$ of the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], adopt the equation-based Einstein and smooth curved Maxwell systems of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]], with the smooth matter quantities and electromagnetic stress of [[def-emg-matter-observables]]. Thus the coupled branch includes the adopted Einstein equation $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=(8\pi G_N/c^4)(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab})$ and Maxwell equations $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, using the fixed local SI signs, units and curvature convention of those suppliers. Their adopted equations remain physical assumptions; neither is deduced here from flat spacetime, variational stationarity, or mathematical structure.

Choose smooth $\rho,\sigma,U$ on $\Omega$, with $\rho\geq0$, $U$ future timelike, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $\sigma=0$ wherever $\rho=0$. Select the pressureless dust closure

$$T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b,\qquad j^a=\sigma U^a.$$

As the matter model, adopt the undivided smooth mass and Lorentz-force equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho U^a)=0,\qquad \rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c,$$

and charge-current conservation $\nabla_aj^a=0$. On each open region $\Omega_+:=\{p\in\Omega:\rho(p)>0\}$ define $\alpha:=\sigma/\rho$. Under the adopted mass continuity and charged-dust forms, [[thm-emg-charged-dust-projection]] gives the exact equivalence between charge-current conservation and transport $U^a\nabla_a\alpha=0$. The ratio is not defined and no division is made on $\rho=0$. The same mathematical supplier gives the stress-exchange equivalence on $\Omega_+$; it supplies no global coupled evolution theorem.

This is a selected classical pressureless, single-stream continuum model. It excludes viscosity, conduction, multistream averaging, spin, point sources, self-field products and a general dust action. The finely fixed charge-to-mass ratio used in the specific ECD solutions of Meinel and Hütten is not a law of this general model. Smooth validity may end at a caustic; no existence, uniqueness, stability, or empirical claim is adopted.

post-emg-charged-fluid-balance.physical_scope: A selected smooth positive-rest-energy perfect-fluid domain coupled through the adopted Einstein–Maxwell equations and matter exchange. The current is either convective or uses a separately selected smooth Ohmic conduction branch. It asserts no global fluid or conducting-fluid evolution, entropy law, or empirical validity.

post-emg-charged-fluid-balance:
## Postulate

On a smooth open state domain $\Omega$ in the spacetime and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], choose $C^1$ rest-energy density $\epsilon>0$, pressure $p$, rest-charge density $\sigma$, and a $C^2$ future-timelike field $U$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The equation-based coupled branch uses [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]] with a smooth symmetric matter tensor and current supplied by this selected fluid model. Adopt the perfect-fluid tensor

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab}$$

and either the convective current $j^a=\sigma U^a$ or a separately specified conduction current $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$. Adopt charge continuity $\nabla_aj^a=0$ and the local matter-exchange balance $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The fields and derivatives are smooth enough for these equations to hold pointwise.

For an optional Ohmic branch, choose a smooth scalar conductivity $\chi\geq0$ in $\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$ and impose $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$ is the rest-frame electric field in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. This is a separate constitutive adoption, not a consequence of covariance or of the Maxwell equations. A smooth equation of state may be supplied on the chosen local state domain; no particular function, relativistic entropy law, causality assertion, or thermodynamic interpretation of $\epsilon,p$ is included here. The stress-projection and comoving work identities follow conditionally from [[thm-emg-charged-fluid-projections]], but no global fluid or conducting-fluid solution theory is asserted.

This postulate adopts a local classical matter branch. It does not presume an unspecified matter action or infer empirical validity from the source literature.

pthm-emg-dust-mass-force-reduction.physical_scope: A conditional local stress/current balance reduction for the selected smooth charged-dust continuum on an open positive-density region. It identifies the exact mass-continuity, charge-transport and Lorentz-force equations and asserts no coupled PDE existence or behavior at zero density.

pthm-emg-dust-mass-force-reduction:
## Statement

Let $\Omega_+\subseteq\Omega$ be an open positive-density region of the charged-dust model in [[post-emg-transported-charged-dust]]. Let $\rho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega_+,\mathbb R)$ with $\rho>0$, let $U\in C^2(\Omega_+,T\Omega_+)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and let the smooth electromagnetic two-form and metric be those of that model. Set $a^b:=U^a\nabla_aU^b$, $T_m^{ab}:=\rho U^aU^b$, and $j^a:=\sigma U^a$.

On $\Omega_+$ the adopted charged-dust matter-exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$ is equivalent to

$$\nabla_a(\rho U^a)=0,\qquad \rho a^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c.$$

Under the mass-continuity equation, $\nabla_aj^a=0$ is equivalent to transport of the charge-to-mass ratio $\alpha:=\sigma/\rho$ along the flow, $U^a\nabla_a\alpha=0$. These are model deductions on $\Omega_+$; the ratio and the divided force law are not defined at zero density. The result supplies no Maxwell or Einstein solution, coupled-field existence theorem, or caustic-avoidance claim.

pthm-emg-fluid-work-heating.physical_scope: A conditional local energy and pressure-force projection for the selected smooth charged perfect fluid. Comoving electromagnetic work is zero for the convective current and is nonnegative for the separately adopted smooth Ohmic law. This is a mechanical balance, not an entropy theorem or global fluid solution.

pthm-emg-fluid-work-heating:
## Statement

Let $\Omega$ be a smooth open state domain of [[post-emg-charged-fluid-balance]]. Assume $\epsilon,p,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$, $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, $F$ is a smooth electromagnetic two-form, and the matter stress and current satisfy the selected fluid closure and exchange equation. Define

$$D:=U^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_aU^a,\qquad a^b:=DU^b,\qquad h^b{}_c:=\delta^b{}_c+\frac{U^bU_c}{c^2},\qquad f^b:=F^b{}_cj^c,\qquad E_U^a:=F^a{}_bU^b.$$

Then the longitudinal work and rest-space force equations are

$$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\theta=-U_bf^b,\qquad \frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}a^b+h^{ba}\nabla_ap=h^b{}_cf^c.$$

For the convective branch $j^a=\sigma U^a$, the comoving electromagnetic work $-U_bf^b$ is zero. For the optional smooth Ohmic branch $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$, $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, with $\chi\geq0$, it is

$$-U_bf^b=\chi\,g(E_U,E_U)\geq0.$$

Here $E_U$ is the rest-frame electric field and the induced metric on $U^\perp$ is positive definite. This is a conditional mechanical energy identity; it does not assert an entropy-production law, equation-of-state evolution, causal constitutive theory, or fluid existence.

pthm-emg-matter-symmetry-charges.physical_scope: Conditional total-stress conservation and finite-domain Killing flux for the selected smooth charged-dust Einstein–Maxwell branch, plus the local gauge-compensated first integral for a separate prescribed-field charged test body. Finite-chain side flux and local-potential conditions are retained; no gravitational-field energy, global charge, self-field, or global trajectory claim is made. The probe branch carries ACω through the published RPM action-equivalence result.

pthm-emg-matter-symmetry-charges:
## Statement

Let $\Omega_+$ be a smooth positive-density region of the selected charged-dust model, and require $F,j,T_m$ to satisfy the smoothness hypotheses of the Maxwell-stress and Killing-current suppliers. Assume the dust fields satisfy the model equations and the conditional matter-exchange identity of [[pthm-emg-dust-mass-force-reduction]], and assume the smooth Maxwell equations of [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. Define $T_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}:=T_m^{ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}$. Let $\xi$ be a smooth Killing field on $\Omega_+$, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, and set $J_\xi^a:=T_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}\xi_b$. For any finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ in $\Omega_+$ with boundary $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, define $\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma):=\int_\Sigma\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g$. Then

$$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ_\xi^a=0,\qquad \mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-\mathcal Q_\xi(B).$$

The two slice charges are equal only when the side flux $\mathcal Q_\xi(B)$ vanishes. This is a matter-plus-electromagnetic stress current, not a local gravitational-energy tensor; no asymptotic or universal global energy is asserted.

There is also the following separate test-body clause. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. On a local potential domain $V\subseteq\Omega_+$, let $A$ be a supplied smooth one-form with $F=dA$ and let $\chi$ be a smooth scalar such that $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\chi$. Let $z:[a,b]\to V$ be a finite $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment, parameterized by proper time $\tau$, with fixed-endpoint variations as in [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]. If the segment is stationary for that adopted action, then [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] gives $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$ for its constant $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and $U=dz/d\tau$. Consequently

$$C_\xi:=m\,g(U,\xi)+q\bigl(A(\xi)-\chi\bigr)$$

is constant along the segment and is invariant under $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$, $\chi\mapsto\chi+\mathcal L_\xi\lambda$. This conditional test-body identity uses no self-field, global potential, trajectory-existence, or Einstein-solution claim.

pthm-emg-matter-energy-conditions.physical_scope: Pointwise observer interpretation of the selected smooth electromagnetic, charged-dust and perfect-fluid stress tensors. Electromagnetic and nonnegative-dust energy conditions are conditional tensor deductions; perfect-fluid conclusions require the exact stated inequalities. No general matter positivity or empirical claim is made.

pthm-emg-matter-energy-conditions:
## Statement

Use the smooth electromagnetic stress, observer contractions and selected matter tensors of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], with $\mu_0>0$ and a future unit observer $n$. The electromagnetic tensor is symmetric and trace-free, and it satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. In a positively oriented orthonormal rest tetrad, with the cross product taken in the oriented Euclidean rest space, its energy density and spatial energy-current components are

$$u=\frac{\epsilon_0|E_n|^2+|B_n|^2/\mu_0}{2},\qquad \mathcal S_n=\frac{E_n\times B_n}{\mu_0c}.$$

For charged dust with $\rho\geq0$, the matter tensor and its sum with the electromagnetic tensor satisfy all four conditions. For a selected perfect-fluid tensor with rest energy density $\epsilon$ and pressure $p$, the exact pointwise conditions on the matter tensor are

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff \epsilon\geq0\text{ and }\epsilon+p\geq0,\qquad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\epsilon+p\geq0,$$

$$\mathrm{SEC}\iff\epsilon+p\geq0\text{ and }\epsilon+3p\geq0,\qquad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\epsilon\geq|p|.$$

If the perfect-fluid tensor satisfies any one of these conditions, adding the electromagnetic tensor preserves that condition. The inequalities are not assumed universally, and adding the electromagnetic tensor to arbitrary matter need not repair a violated condition.

ex-emg-ml-b03.physical_scope: Two exact pointwise electromagnetic-stress calculations in an orthonormal observer frame: a pure magnetic field has anisotropic principal stresses, and crossed equal-normalized electric and magnetic fields saturate the DEC flux bound. These are ideal local/test-background calculations, not measurements or full coupled Einstein–Maxwell solutions.
